body.statement:
Let \(P_n\) and \(P\) be probability laws, let \(E_n,E\) be events, and let \(A_n(x)\subseteq E_n\) and \(A(x)\subseteq E\) be nested events indexed by \(x\in\mathbb R\). If \(P(E)\ge m>\delta\), \(\lvert P_n(E_n)-P(E)\rvert\le\delta\), and \(\sup_x\lvert P_n(A_n(x))-P(A(x))\rvert\le\delta\), then
\[
\sup_x\left\lvert P_n\{A_n(x)\mid E_n\}-P\{A(x)\mid E\}\right\rvert\le \frac{2\delta}{m-\delta}.
\]
If the conditional limit cdf has density at least \(g>0\) on a radius-\(a\) neighborhood of its \(p\)-quantile and the left side is at most \(e<ag\), then the generalized \(p\)-quantile differs from the limiting quantile by at most \(e/g\).
body.proof_tex:
Put \(p_n=P_n(E_n)\), \(p=P(E)\), \(a_n(x)=P_n(A_n(x))\), and \(a(x)=P(A(x))\).  The assumptions give \(p_n\ge m-\delta>0\), and nesting gives \(0\le a(x)\le p\).  Therefore
\[
\left|\frac{a_n(x)}{p_n}-\frac{a(x)}p\right|
\le\frac{|a_n(x)-a(x)|}{p_n}
+\frac{a(x)|p_n-p|}{p_np}
\le\frac{2\delta}{m-\delta}.
\]
Taking the supremum proves the conditional-cdf inequality.  For quantiles, let \(q\) be the limiting \(p\)-quantile and let \(F_n,F\) be the conditional cdfs.  If \(0<t<a\), the density lower bound yields \(F(q-t)\le p-gt\) and \(F(q+t)\ge p+gt\).  When \(t>e/g\), uniform cdf error gives \(F_n(q-t)<p<F_n(q+t)\), so the generalized quantile \(q_n=\inf\{x:F_n(x)\ge p\}\) satisfies \(q-t<q_n\le q+t\).  Letting \(t\downarrow e/g\) proves \(|q_n-q|\le e/g\).
body.justification: The elementary numerator--denominator inequality makes every conditioning division and quantile transfer explicit.
body.gap: Unconditional convergence alone does not control selected laws when event probabilities are small.
body.consumer: Both sampling and Fisher-reference transfers use one auditable error map.
